title: Supreme Court to examine 'lifetime immunity' for election commissioners
dek: The court issued notice on petitions by RJD MP Manoj Jha and advocate Arun Agrawal against Section 16 of the 2023 law, which bars cases against serving and former commissioners. Hearing on 18 December.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine whether the legal shield given to the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners is constitutional. It issued notice to the Centre on two new petitions that say the protection amounts to lifelong immunity from prosecution and civil suits.

The petitions were filed by Rashtriya Janata Dal Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Kumar Jha and the activist-advocate Arun Agrawal. A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana tagged them with an earlier challenge by the NGO Lok Prahari and listed all of them for hearing on 18 December, reports said. One report said that the court asked the Centre to respond within four weeks.

## What the law says

The petitions challenge Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. The provision was not in the bill as first introduced. It was added through a government amendment, numbered as a new clause 15A, before the Rajya Sabha passed the bill on 12 December 2023. The amendment notice reads:

> "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function."

The Lok Sabha passed the bill on 21 December 2023.

## What the petitioners argue

Jha's petition, Manoj Kumar Jha v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 1404 of 2026), argues that the words "is or was" give commissioners protection for life, and that the section is "unconstitutional and arbitrary", according to reports. It says the immunity is wider than that given to the President, governors, legislators or judges of constitutional courts, and that Article 324 of the Constitution, which sets up the Election Commission, provides for no such protection. The petition also argues that the provision closely follows the Judges (Protection) Act, 1985, but leaves out that law's safeguard allowing the government or courts to proceed against a judge. It says the provision violates several articles of the Constitution, including Articles 14 and 21.

Agrawal's petition argues that the commissioners' tenure is already protected by the Constitution, so blanket immunity is not needed, and that the section takes away remedies from voters, candidates and citizens who may be harmed by wrongdoing. Advocate Fauzia Shakil appeared for Jha and advocate Neha Rathi for Agrawal.

The government has not yet filed its reply.

## What the court said

The Chief Justice discouraged the filing of more petitions on the same point. He said repeated filings delay the completion of pleadings and distract from the main case, reports said. If someone believes an important point has been missed, the bench said, they should ask to be added to the pending case rather than file a new one.

## Background

The court issued notice on Lok Prahari's petition in January 2026 but declined at that stage to put Section 16 on hold. Reports have also said that the court issued notice on 13 October on a challenge by the Association for Democratic Reforms, which seeks the revival of civil and criminal cases against serving and former commissioners that ended after the section came into force.

The case comes at a time of open conflict between the opposition and the Election Commission. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has drawn opposition objections over the scale of deletions in several states. Separate petitions over the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar are before the same bench, which on Tuesday organised those cases into nine groups for hearing.

## What happens next

The Centre has four weeks to reply. All the challenges to Section 16 will be heard together on 18 December. Until the court rules, the section remains in force.
